title: Silicon-Modified Biochar in Sustainable and Climate-Resilient Agroecosystems
content: Silicon-rich and silicon-modified biochars (Si-BCs) are amendments for sustainable soil management, contaminant remediation, and climate-resilient agriculture. This review examines four production routes: direct pyrolysis of silicon-rich biomass, pre-pyrolysis modification, co-pyrolysis with silicon-rich feedstocks, and post-pyrolysis modification. It assesses how feedstock composition and processing affect silicon speciation, structural accessibility, dissolution kinetics and silicon transfer to the soil–plant system. It highlights analytical limitations and the distinction between total, extractable and plant-available silicon. Evidence is synthesized on Si-BC effects on soil structure, water retention, nutrient dynamics, microbial communities and plant tolerance to abiotic stress. The review also examines mechanisms of potentially toxic element immobilisation and transformation, as well as potential greenhouse gas mitigation and carbon sequestration. Outcomes depend on biochar properties, soil conditions and management; differences in experimental designs and evaluation methods hinder comparison and generalization. Research priorities include standardized characterisation and silicon-release protocols, controlled studies separating silicon-specific effects from those of the biochar matrix and co-introduced constituents and long-term field validation. Life-cycle impacts, production costs, scalability and environmental safety also require assessment. Overall, total silicon content alone is a poor predictor of performance; silicon speciation, accessibility and release kinetics govern its effective transfer from biochar to the soil–plant system.
